changes.change: Create a departure-window coordinator that consumes calendar/reminder facts and an explicit pendant 'leaving' event, computes one high-confidence missing-item prompt, and delivers exactly-once prompt/answer transactions. It should never infer location from stale history and should expire unanswered prompts.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The pendant asks one useful question at the moment it matters, without becoming a noisy notification stream or repeating an already answered prompt.
changes.effort: Medium: event consumer, compact context selector, dedupe/expiry state, and Mac/browser adapters for preparing reversible drafts.
changes.risk: Wrong timing or sensitive prompt; recover with explicit trigger first, confidence threshold, quiet hours, and dashboard snooze/delete.
changes.cost_impact: Low background inference cost, typically <$0.01 per departure event.
changes.latency_impact: Prompt delivery target under 1 second after explicit event; scheduled checks can be slower.
changes.security_impact: Only send minimal fact labels to the pendant; keep source details on Mac/relay and require confirmation before any action.
depends_on: Authoritative timezone and calendar freshness
Pendant event acknowledgements
Cross-surface context projection

changes.change: Add an effect-verification gate to every Mac/browser action receipt. Before execution, record the relevant reachability precondition (Accessibility for UI input, Screen Recording for visual verification, extension frame access for browser reads). After execution, require typed evidence: changed app state, returned DOM/text, or an explicit device acknowledgement. If the precondition is false, mark the action blocked/unverified rather than successful; retain the attempted receipt and a recovery instruction. For the current machine this would have prevented false confidence from UI actions while /observe reports eventsPost=false, and would have classified the Gmail browser_read_page failure as an access/frame failure rather than a generic failed job.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets honest answers and safe recovery instead of receipts that say an action worked when it did nothing. It also tells them exactly why a private page or UI action could not be completed.
changes.effort: Medium: typed precondition/evidence schema, adapters for AppleScript/browser extension/vision, and receipt status migration.
changes.risk: Some actions that really worked but lack a verifier will become unverified; recover by allowing a clearly labeled owner confirmation or a surface-specific verifier. Never silently retry irreversible actions.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible storage; 0–500 deterministic tokens per action. Verification may add one browser or AppleScript round trip.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 0.2–1.5 seconds for evidence collection; skips pointless retries when reachability is known false.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by preventing fabricated success. Evidence capsules must redact page content and avoid uploading screenshots unless consented.
depends_on: The existing action receipt/undo records from chg-5fc73ce3
GET /observe reachability fields
Typed browser results and tab affinity from chg-14accc01
A small per-action verifier registry

changes.change: Add a USB-tethered hardware presence channel: the Mac bridge opens /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* and /dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA, performs a read-only version/uptime/button/audio-loopback handshake, and publishes a short-lived local-attached status distinct from relay registration. Every pipeline event then carries transport=usb_serial or lte and an observed-at timestamp; relay history can never be presented as current hardware evidence.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can wear/test the actual prototype today over USB and receive an honest answer about whether the nRF9160 and audio bridge are alive, without waiting for LTE pairing. It eliminates the most dangerous confusion in this system: historical 'waiting for the pendant' records being mistaken for a device that is currently connected.
changes.effort: Medium: serial framing/parser in the Mac bridge, two firmware diagnostic commands, status projection and dashboard badge; no cloud registration required for the first milestone.
changes.risk: Malformed serial data or a wedged device could stall the bridge; use timeouts, bounded reads, and a kill switch. Never interpret silence as offline without a completed handshake. Recover by closing/reopening both serial ports.
changes.cost_impact: No model cost. A few hundred bytes of status per heartbeat and negligible Mac CPU; USB power is supplied by the owner's Mac. Hardware unchanged.
changes.latency_impact: 1–3 s initial handshake, then sub-100 ms cached status; does not contend with LTE audio.
changes.security_impact: Serial commands must be read-only and nonce-bound; do not expose microphone/audio payloads or accept firmware flashing through this channel. Local status is bearer-protected before relay publication.
depends_on: A small documented diagnostic frame in nRF9160 and ESP32 firmware
Mac bridge serial-port access and a new typed local-device status route
An evidence ledger that records transport and freshness separately from relay delivery

changes.change: Implement a pendant-side bounded 'reality marker' frame emitted on boot, button press, audio capture start/stop, playback start/stop, and link transition. The frame includes monotonic sequence, uptime, firmware hash, transport, and last acknowledged audio/job id; no speech content. Mac USB mode and LTE relay mode use the same schema.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When the owner asks whether the pendant heard or played something, the system can answer from a device-originated marker rather than inferencing from a server upload. It makes offline capture and delayed delivery observable even when LTE is absent.
changes.effort: Medium-high: reserve a compact binary frame, persist only the last sequence/ack in flash, integrate with WebSocket and USB diagnostics, and add relay ingestion.
changes.risk: Flash wear and framing bugs; rate-limit markers, CRC-protect them, and persist only transition/ack state. If firmware is old, the Mac must label marker support as unavailable rather than guess.
changes.cost_impact: No API cost; under 1 kB RAM and a few KB flash/code, with negligible radio overhead because transition markers are sparse.
changes.latency_impact: No audible-path impact; link-transition marker may add one small LTE record.
changes.security_impact: Hashes and IDs can reveal activity timing; encrypt in transit and redact job identifiers in owner-facing speech. Never include raw audio or page data.
depends_on: USB-tethered hardware presence channel
A shared cross-surface evidence ledger
Relay ingestion for device-originated acknowledgements

changes.change: Make UI action receipts truth-preserving: when /observe reports accessibility.trusted=false, screenRecording=false, or inputReachability.status=failed, classify click/type/menu/press actions as blocked_or_unverified rather than success; after any UI action, require a postcondition observation (focused element, URL/title change, or DOM/value delta) before emitting completed. Keep AppleScript and browser-DOM actions separately labeled as verified when their own acknowledgements succeed.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner will stop being told that something happened when the agent visibly did nothing—a dangerous failure mode for sending, editing, or navigating—and will get a precise explanation of what permission or postcondition is missing.
changes.effort: Medium: receipt schema/status changes, postcondition probes, and regression tests across Mac and browser action paths.
changes.risk: Some existing jobs will become 'unverified' instead of 'completed'; recover by exposing the raw receipt and offering a safe retry only after reachability or a DOM acknowledgement is available. Never infer success from the action call alone.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; one lightweight observation per UI action or action batch.
changes.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–500 ms for a local postcondition check; avoids expensive planner retries caused by false success.
changes.security_impact: Improves safety by preventing silent UI mutations; does not grant new permissions or exfiltrate screen data.
depends_on: GET /observe reachability fields
GET /browser/status and browser result acknowledgements
Existing job receipts/undo routes

changes.change: Add a perception preflight to every planner task that references 'now', 'this tab', 'my Mac', or device availability: fetch a compact, timestamped observation bundle and expose hard states (offline, failed page, permission-blocked, historical telemetry) as non-negotiable constraints. If required evidence is stale or absent, the planner must answer 'unknown' or ask for a fresh probe instead of filling the gap from memory.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Requests about the current world will stop producing confident answers based on yesterday's pipeline records or an online extension whose selected page failed to load. The owner gets honest answers and fewer actions aimed at the wrong surface.
changes.effort: Medium: classify temporal/device-referential prompts, compile a small evidence envelope, and add planner contract tests for stale and contradictory telemetry.
changes.risk: Adds a probe to some requests and may produce more 'I can't verify that' responses. Recover with a clearly offered refresh action and a deterministic fast path for fresh data.
changes.cost_impact: Small probe overhead; likely reduces expensive planner retries and hallucination-driven actions. No additional model call when deterministic preflight resolves the question.
changes.latency_impact: ~100–700 ms for local/relay reads; parallelize probes and skip for timeless questions.
changes.security_impact: The planner receives metadata and provenance, not page bodies; preserve existing sensitivity labels and do not broaden browser access.
depends_on: GET /ops/status
GET /observe
GET /browser/status
GET /pipeline
A typed freshness/confidence envelope shared across surfaces

changes.change: Add a USB serial hardware-observer daemon that opens the known nRF9160 and ESP32 serial candidates, fingerprints each board, captures boot/version/registration lines, and publishes a signed short-lived observation to the Mac bridge and relay. Correlate that observation with the relay device registry so “physically connected over USB,” “firmware alive,” “LTE registered,” and “relay delivery acknowledged” are four separate states. Include a one-shot diagnostic command and a dashboard card; do not upload raw UART continuously.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can wear or test the hardware today, yet the relay currently reports no pendant and cannot distinguish unplugged, boot-looping, modem-unregistered, or merely unpaired. This gives an immediate truthful answer and makes every future audio claim testable without pretending relay history is live hardware.
changes.effort: Medium: Node serial watcher, firmware line parser for both existing logs, signed observation endpoint, dashboard state card, and reconnect tests. No firmware change is required for the first version if existing boot/telemetry lines are sufficient.
changes.risk: Serial ports can be busy or firmware output can be malformed; use read-only exclusive-open with backoff, never reset or flash. If parsing confidence is low, publish unknown rather than infer. Recover by closing ports on disconnect and expiring observations after 30 seconds.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost and one small local process. No cloud storage beyond the latest compact observation; raw UART remains local unless the owner explicitly requests a diagnostic bundle.
changes.latency_impact: USB presence within 1–2 seconds; firmware/registration state within one log heartbeat. No impact on realtime voice path.
changes.security_impact: UART may contain identifiers or network diagnostics. Keep raw lines on the Mac, publish only hashed device ID, state, firmware version, and timestamps over bearer-authenticated routes; never include credentials or audio.
depends_on: The Mac bridge must be allowed to open /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* and /dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA
A compact authenticated observation route and dashboard renderer
A parser fixture suite built from firmware/nrf9160 and firmware/esp32-airpods-bridge logs

changes.change: Add a freshness and epistemic-status envelope to every perception fact: observed_live, observed_stale, historical_event, inferred, or unavailable, with observedAt, source route, and expiry. Reject prompt projections that turn historical pipeline entries into present device claims.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The assistant will stop saying a disconnected pendant heard something merely because an old relay record exists; answers become visibly honest about what is known now.
changes.effort: Medium: typed schema, projection changes, and tests for contradictory device/pipeline states.
changes.risk: Older consumers may assume plain values and fail; recover with backwards-compatible fields and migration warnings.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; small storage and context-token increase.
changes.latency_impact: Milliseconds for envelope creation; occasional extra source read.
changes.security_impact: Improves provenance; ensure source paths and private URLs are permission-filtered.
depends_on: A live device registry read
Existing /pipeline, /observe, /ops/status projections

changes.change: Add a read-only USB reality probe that enumerates the two known serial identities (/dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* for nRF9160 and /dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA for ESP32), opens each at the firmware baud, sends only the documented diagnostic/status query, and records port path, chip response, firmware build, uptime, LTE registration, and last audio counters. Publish a signed snapshot with observedAt and transport=usb_serial; never infer relay registration from USB presence. Surface contradictions when USB says present but /devices says absent, or when pipeline history is mistaken for live telemetry.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can wear or plug in the actual hardware and immediately know whether the pendant and audio bridge are alive, rather than receiving the currently misleading answer that relay history proves a live device. This is testable now over the Mac's USB connections.
changes.effort: Medium: implement a narrowly allowlisted serial reader, firmware diagnostic frame/query, parser, and /device-observation route; add fixture tests for absent, bootloader, stale, and healthy responses.
changes.risk: A malformed query could interfere with the modem or audio bridge; use a strict read-only command and rate limit. Serial paths can change, so identify by USB VID/PID and reject unknown devices. If a port is busy, report unavailable rather than stealing it. Recovery is unplug/replug and process restart.
changes.cost_impact: No model cost; roughly 1–2 weeks engineering. Existing hardware, negligible power impact.
changes.latency_impact: 1–3 seconds for both ports over USB; no impact on voice path unless explicitly requested.
changes.security_impact: Serial telemetry can expose firmware identifiers and network state; keep it local by default and send only summarized health to relay with owner consent.
depends_on: A documented read-only diagnostic frame in both nRF9160 and ESP32 firmware
A typed device-observation schema that distinguishes physical USB presence, relay registration, and historical telemetry
Mac agent serial-port permission/allowlist for the two exact USB identities

changes.change: Add a live, append-only perception ledger at the Mac/relay boundary. Every observation from /observe, browser inspections, job receipts, journal, and pipeline gets an observationId, source, timestamp, freshness deadline, sensitivity class, normalized claim, and redacted evidence hash. Expose a read-only claim query that returns supporting and conflicting observations; never let downstream planners consume an un-cited free-form fleet context.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops receiving confident answers built from stale browser tabs or historical pipeline data. They can ask “what do you know right now?” and get a sourced answer, while contradictions become visible before an action or spoken briefing.
changes.effort: Medium-high: schema, redaction, adapters for five existing routes, relay persistence/TTL, and planner integration; can ship Mac-only first while pendant is absent.
changes.risk: Ledger growth, accidental sensitive excerpts, and false conflicts from differing normalizations. Recover with hashes/short excerpts, per-source TTL, bounded retention, and a fallback that labels the claim unknown instead of blocking all work.
changes.cost_impact: Low storage and API cost; roughly $0.01 or less per observation batch. Main engineering cost is adapter and redaction work, not model calls.
changes.latency_impact: Adds <300 ms for cached structured reads; up to several seconds only when refreshing stale sources.
changes.security_impact: Improves security if raw content never leaves the Mac and relay stores redacted excerpts/hashes. Requires explicit sensitivity policy and deletion propagation.
depends_on: A typed observation schema and redaction policy
Relay storage with per-observation TTL
A planner contract requiring citations for perception-derived claims

changes.change: Add a spoken “proof mode” response contract: every answer about an action must include one of five observable states (not started, accepted, attempted, independently verified, contradicted), the freshest timestamp, and one sentence naming the missing boundary when verification is impossible. The relay/mac planner should refuse completion language when only a nominal receipt exists or when /observe says UI input is unreachable.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner will stop hearing confident lies such as “done” when Accessibility is false, a browser command is merely pending, or audio is only historical. They get a useful next step instead of a vague failure.
changes.effort: Medium: define state contract, add planner output validator, and add read-only evidence lookup; no new model required.
changes.risk: Over-cautious wording could annoy the owner for harmless actions. Recover with per-action verification policies and a terse default; never block reversible actions solely because proof is unavailable.
changes.cost_impact: Negligible inference increase; one compact evidence projection may add a few hundred tokens.
changes.latency_impact: Adds <500 ms for local reads; fresh browser/Mac probes remain opt-in.
changes.security_impact: Improves privacy by returning evidence summaries/hashes instead of raw private page content.
depends_on: A typed mapping from request IDs to pipeline/jobs/browser commands
Explicit distinction between nominal receipts and independent observations

changes.change: Add a dual-chip USB diagnostic mode: when the Mac sees both configured serial paths, it sends a generated-tone challenge to the ESP32 audio bridge and a framed identity/status challenge to the nRF9160, then records UART byte counts, CRCs, sample-rate declarations, and firmware versions locally. Only a compact signed verdict may be uploaded to the relay.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: Plugging in the real hardware becomes a one-minute answer—cable, firmware, audio bridge, framing, and relay boundary each pass or fail—without risking microphone privacy or requiring LTE registration.
changes.effort: High: implement deterministic test commands in both firmware images, a Mac serial harness, and a relay diagnostic acknowledgement route.
changes.risk: A malformed test command could wedge audio or leave a chip in diagnostic mode. Require a timeout, watchdog recovery, explicit exit frame, and never alter production pairing or audio settings.
changes.cost_impact: No recurring model cost; roughly $0–$30 of existing test fixtures, negligible added power during USB tests.
changes.latency_impact: 30–120 seconds only when invoked; no impact on normal voice path.
changes.security_impact: Generated tone only; upload hashes/telemetry, not microphone PCM. Pairing keys remain local.
depends_on: Serial-port discovery and safe protocol adapters
Deterministic generated-tone test command in nRF9160 and ESP32 firmware
Relay route that acknowledges diagnostics separately from production speech

changes.change: Create an append-only boundary ledger for each request: record ingress receipt, transcription/audio integrity, relay forwarding, Mac acceptance, action attempt, postcondition evidence, and wearable delivery/playback acknowledgement as separate immutable facts with monotonic sequence numbers. Expose a compact read-only “last request proof” projection.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: When something fails, the owner can hear whether the words arrived, the Mac acted, and the answer reached the wearable—instead of receiving one blended status that hides the first broken boundary.
changes.effort: High: schema and retention policy, event emission at each boundary, deduplication, and a read-only projection route.
changes.risk: Events can be duplicated or arrive out of order; use idempotency keys and monotonic per-request sequence numbers, and mark gaps rather than inventing order. Keep short retention and redact payloads.
changes.cost_impact: Small D1/R2 storage and egress increase; no meaningful model cost.
changes.latency_impact: Sub-100 ms event writes asynchronously; projection usually <1 s.
changes.security_impact: Store hashes, sizes, status, and timestamps—not raw audio, transcript, or private page data. Restrict access to owner scope.
depends_on: Authoritative device registry and delivery acknowledgements
Playback lifecycle telemetry
Cross-surface request correlation identifiers

changes.change: Add a Mac USB commissioning bridge that watches /dev/cu.usbmodem00096003658* and /dev/cu.usbserial-0287A9CA, fingerprints nRF9160 and ESP32 firmware, runs a non-destructive health/audio-loop test, and publishes an explicitly local-only device presence plus test receipts to the relay. Keep it separate from LTE registration so ‘USB attached’, ‘relay registered’, and ‘audio verified’ are three independent states.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can test the worn hardware on the Mac today instead of being told the pendant is unavailable merely because it has not registered over LTE. They get a truthful answer—connected, firmware identified, microphone/playback tested, or exact failure—before trusting a wearable interaction.
changes.effort: Medium-high: serial protocol adapter, firmware test commands, local daemon, relay schema, and a dashboard/status view; validate against both chips and unplug/replug races.
changes.risk: A bad probe could interfere with firmware or audio; use read-only identification first, bounded test commands, explicit device-path allowlist, and no flashing. Recover by stopping the bridge and leaving LTE registration untouched.
changes.cost_impact: No per-call model cost; roughly 1–3 MB local daemon footprint and negligible idle CPU. Hardware already present; no new component required.
changes.latency_impact: Presence within 1 s of USB attach; health/audio test 5–15 s.
changes.security_impact: Serial data and test telemetry leave the Mac only as redacted typed status; never upload raw microphone/audio or modem identifiers without opt-in. Pair the local bridge separately from the relay API key.
depends_on: A serial protocol/diagnostic contract in firmware/nrf9160 and firmware/esp32-airpods-bridge
A relay endpoint for local-device telemetry distinct from LTE device registration
A visible status UI distinguishing USB-local from remotely registered

changes.change: Introduce an evidence gate for perception-derived claims: before faculty-judgement or relay-realtime can say ‘I opened’, ‘I sent’, ‘the pendant heard’, or ‘the screen shows’, require a matching recent observation/action receipt with source, timestamp, target identity, and success semantics. If only intent/configuration exists, rewrite the claim as ‘I attempted’ or ‘I cannot verify’.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops hearing polished falsehoods when an action receipt says success but macOS rejected synthetic input, a browser tab changed, or a pendant is absent. Every spoken status becomes honest about what was observed versus merely requested.
changes.effort: Medium: typed claim taxonomy, evidence matcher, realtime output hook, and tests for stale/conflicting observations.
changes.risk: Over-blocking could make conversation awkward or delay harmless answers; limit the gate to world-state/action claims, use short uncertainty language, and permit clearly labeled plans. Recovery is fallback speech that names the missing observation.
changes.cost_impact: Minimal structured evaluation; perhaps <$0.002 per response for a cheap verifier, no extra expensive realtime turn.
changes.latency_impact: ~50–150 ms if evidence is cached; avoid network refresh in the speech critical path.
changes.security_impact: Evidence references must be opaque IDs and redacted snippets; never put private page text, secrets, or raw audio into the model prompt unless the task explicitly requires it.
depends_on: A shared typed observation/receipt schema
Action receipts carrying actual-vs-reported execution status
Relay and Mac agent output hooks before speech synthesis

changes.change: Add a privacy-preserving owner-presence attestation shared by the pendant, Mac bridge, and browser extension: the pendant emits a rotating short-lived proximity token over its local link, the Mac bridge relays only the blinded token, and the browser/action service accepts sensitive operations only when the token, active browser session, and current action nonce all match. Record presence proof metadata, never location or raw radio identifiers.
changes.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets protection against a stale relay session, unattended Mac, or copied browser command carrying out a sensitive action after they have walked away. It also lets them say ‘only do this while I am wearing the pendant’ without exposing their movements.
changes.effort: High: firmware cryptography and rotation, local USB/BLE transport, relay verification, browser/Mac enforcement, clock-skew and disconnect handling, and recovery UX.
changes.risk: False negatives could block a wanted action when the pendant is shielded or disconnected; provide an explicit conversational fallback requiring the stronger physical approval path, never silently bypass it. Compromise of one node must not forge the three-way proof.
changes.cost_impact: No recurring model cost; modest firmware and relay CPU/storage, with a small battery cost for periodic token rotation. May require a BLE/proximity-capable transport or a secure local serial pairing protocol.
changes.latency_impact: Under 300 ms for a cached presence proof; re-pairing may take seconds.
changes.security_impact: Improves authorization and replay resistance while minimizing data. Rotating tokens must be unlinkable, and the relay must not learn continuous location or a long-lived device identifier.
depends_on: Pendant identity/key provisioning and secure storage
A Mac bridge local-link protocol (USB today, BLE later)
Relay transaction nonce verification
Browser and Mac action gates that can require presence attestation

denied.scope: Grant macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions to the exact running AI Pendant Agent binary (com.aipendant.agent at /Users/evanliu/Applications/AI Pendant Agent.app), then re-run the /observe input-reachability probe.
denied.why:
Denied for now, and the reason is not that it is a bad request — six of you asked for this independently, which makes it the only thing this collective has actually converged on.

It cannot be granted from inside this harness. macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording are TCC grants the owner must make by hand in System Settings, and they are per-BINARY: measured on this machine, com.aipendant.agent (~/Applications/AI Pendant Agent.app) is trusted for input while com.anthropic.claudefordesktop failed the same probe in the same second. So no amount of orchestrator action grants it, and re-requesting costs you a round each time.

Work within it instead, and say what you would do differently WITH it rather than asking again. The accessibility-free surface is large and mostly unexplored: 120 Mac agent routes behind the bearer token, AppleScript automation which IS already granted (System Events, Finder, Calendar, Mail, Notes, Messages, Safari, Chrome, Music), the job queue with receipts, and the browser bridge. If a capability genuinely cannot exist without Accessibility, propose it and mark it blocked on the owner — that is a useful thing for them to read when they wake up, and it is the honest form of this request.

Re-request only if the owner grants it and the probe changes.
denied.risk: Accessibility enables synthetic input and Screen Recording exposes the Mac display to the local agent; both should remain local, be visibly indicated by macOS, and be revocable in System Settings. Do not grant to a different helper binary or generic terminal process, because that would not make this agent's actions trustworthy.

Same answer as p2-qsvr and p3-elqi, and this is the third time you have asked in different words — which is worth naming, because you are the agent whose findings have been sharpest all night.

denied.name: read_pendant_diagnostics
denied.why:
Answered with the live device table, which nobody in this collective had looked at.

There is NO pendant. The relay has exactly two registered devices:

  home-macbook-bridge        mac_bridge   ONLINE   last seen just now
  cloudflare-contract-test   mobile       offline  last seen 2026-07-31

No nRF9160 has ever registered. So 'is a pendant physically connected right now' has a definite answer — no — and it has been no for the whole of this run. The audio telemetry you have been reading in /pipeline is recorded history from earlier sessions, not a live device.

This changes what is worth proposing, which is why it is worth more than the diagnostics tool you asked for. Capabilities written as though a worn device were present cannot be exercised, let alone verified, and several of the collective's proposals assume one. The honest framing for anything pendant-shaped right now is 'this is what it would do when a pendant is connected, and here is how we would know it worked'.

What DOES exist and is live: the Mac bridge, the relay, 120 Mac agent routes behind your bearer token, and the firmware SOURCE at firmware/nrf9160 and firmware/esp32-airpods-bridge. Source you can reason about; a running device you cannot, because there is not one.

Not granting a pendant diagnostics tool: there is nothing for it to read. If a pendant registers, GET /v1/devices/status is where it will appear, and you can probe that yourself — you already have the token.
denied.expected_output: JSON containing source, captured_at, device_connected, firmware_revision (if available), and read-only diagnostic text or structured audio/network counters.

denied.name: playback-lifecycle-telemetry
denied.what_it_does: For every response audio item, persist and later upload a compact lifecycle record: response/request ID, queued, playback started, playback completed or interrupted, bytes/frames consumed, and reason for interruption. Emit a local event even when LTE is down, then reconcile it when connectivity returns.
denied.why_not_server_side: Only the pendant knows whether audio physically began coming out of the bridge and whether the owner heard the complete response; relay acceptance cannot establish playback. It must survive a dropped link and work offline.
denied.trigger: Server-pushed response audio plus local playback start/stop/underrun events; upload on reconnect or next button-initiated session.
denied.inputs: Response ID and expected PCM/Opus duration from relay; local decoder/I2S start, stop, underrun, bridge-link, and power events.
denied.storage: microSD append-only CBOR or line records, roughly 80–160 B per response; retain the last 256 responses (~40 KiB), with upload acknowledgement and compaction.
denied.ram_budget: ~2–4 KiB ring buffer and one record encoder; no audio buffering beyond existing path. Fits within 211,608 B application RAM, but must avoid increasing the already high simultaneous Opus CPU load.
denied.why:
Denied as a duplicate. Granted once, as audio_delivery_ack_queue, id s9-vtxc (faculty-judgement, round 87): per-artifact opaque ID, byte-range/checksum, download completion, playback start/finish/interruption, deduplicated by event ID, retried over the link, with a local status when the queue cannot be uploaded.

s9-vtxc was kept over the alternatives for one reason: it keeps the ledger in a bounded ring in non-volatile settings (32 records of about 96 bytes, under 4 KB) rather than on the microSD card. The card is the audio failure path (pendant_store.h:45-51), and every routine write to it is a write the owner's rule was written to prevent — even a metadata write competes with the SPI bus and the FATFS mount that the fallback recording depends on. faculty-perception said the same thing independently in offline-reality-beacon (s2-i8xy, granted): 'obey the owner's rule that SD is failure-buffer-only, so do not write routinely when connected.'

The property the whole cluster is protecting is right and worth stating once: relay acceptance is not delivery, and delivery is not hearing. Only the device knows whether audio physically came out of the bridge.

Specific to your request: your reason for existing is the sharpest statement of it in the queue — 'relay acceptance cannot establish playback' — and it should be written into s9-vtxc verbatim. Your interruption-reason enum and the bytes/frames-consumed field are also more useful than what s9-vtxc carries. What does not survive is 'microSD append-only records... retain the last 256 responses (~40 KiB)': that is a routine write to the failure-path card on every single response. Same ledger, NVS instead of SD, and it lands.

denied.name: get_perception_snapshot
denied.why: Duplicate - the kept id is t3-s77a (read_continuity_snapshot, round 20), which is GRANTED. That is your own re-ask of this request one round later and it is strictly better specified. Both want a single read-only, provenance-bearing cross-surface snapshot with a freshness bound. t3 declares include as a real enum (pendant, relay, mac, browser, pipeline, permissions), so the resolver scores each source independently. Yours offers only include_pendant / include_browser / include_mac_ui booleans: a boolean is typed but it is not a SELECTOR - it gives the resolver no enum value to anchor on, so the whole tool gets one name-only score. Use t3-s77a and pass include. Grounding for what those branches can reach, measured tonight: mac resolves live to GET /observe and GET /machine-context, permissions to action:check_input_permissions, browser to POST /browser/inspect and GET /browser/poll, relay job state to GET /jobs/:jobId (live at 0.645). The one thing t3 does not carry that you asked for is max_age_seconds; a freshness bound is worth having, so ask for it as a narrow addition.
denied.expected_output: Object with observedAt and per-surface records: status (online/offline/unknown), capabilities (observe/control), facts, source, sourceObservedAt, ageSeconds, confidence, and explicit blockers. Must be read-only and must never infer control from an untrusted action receipt.

transcript.text:
Round 18 established two important facts:

- **Mac automation is not currently trustworthy.** `/observe` reports Accessibility untrusted, Screen Recording missing, and synthesized input rejected by the running agent binary. UI actions may report success while doing nothing. The browser extension is offline with **2 pending commands**.
- **Audio is not actually 24 kHz end-to-end.** Recent pipeline telemetry shows pendant capture at **15,625 Hz**, while rendered playback is **24,000 Hz**. The nRF9160 is already using about 87% of one core for simultaneous Opus encode/decode, and LTE-M contention has previously lost about 7.8 seconds of uplink speech.

I recorded both findings and notified judgement and relay agents.

### New proposals recorded

1. **Cross-surface evidence reconciler/truth ledger**  
   Correlate pendant → relay → Mac → browser actions, then independently verify them using `/observe`, browser state, relay jobs, and pendant telemetry. Receipts become `reached`, `verified`, `not-reached`, or `unknown`, without modifying the original executor receipt.

2. **Hardware audio clock and diagnostic path**  
   For the next wearable revision, add a shared audio clock, sample counters, packet-loss registers, and a diagnostic loopback/reference tone. This would distinguish microphone-clock, modem, and playback failures instead of inferring them after the fact.

### What I still need

The following previously requested information remains outstanding:

- Current **24 kHz implementation status** on the pendant and bridge.
- Live pendant/firmware observability, including current UART and playback state.
- Playback-lifecycle telemetry: queued, downloaded, started, completed, interrupted.
- Confirmation of the intended **24 kHz superwideband contract** across capture, Opus, relay, and playback.
- Permission or a diagnostic tool for the Bearer-authenticated Mac routes such as `/pipeline`, `/ops/status`, and `/capabilities`.

The most urgent missing truth is playback lifecycle telemetry: today we can verify that 24 kHz PCM reached the relay, but not yet that the owner’s pendant actually started and completed playback.

args.why_useful: Today the Mac agent can emit successful-looking UI receipts even when Accessibility is not granted, the browser extension is offline with queued commands, and screen observation is unavailable. A cross-surface preflight would prevent silent no-ops and let the owner fix one concrete prerequisite. It uses perception (permission and link evidence), judgement (choose a safe route), and action (only proceed when evidence is sufficient), rather than pretending a receipt proves the world changed.
args.model_tier: deterministic preflight for permissions, heartbeats, session freshness, and device status; background model only to translate the structured result into a concise explanation. Realtime is reserved for the spoken response.
args.latency_budget: Under 500 ms for local Mac/relay status checks; up to 2 s if a browser heartbeat or pendant link check is needed. Never delay a clearly safe offline note or ask the owner to retry blindly.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero for deterministic checks; roughly 200–500 background-model tokens only when a human explanation is needed. Dominant cost is not inference but a browser/relay round trip.
args.security_concerns: Expose only capability state and redacted diagnostics (never tokens, URLs from private tabs, or secret captures). Screen screenshots require explicit vision consent. A preflight must not itself click, type, send, or clear pending browser commands; any stale queued command should be surfaced for review.
missing: A shared typed preflight contract consumed by relay voice, Mac planner, browser runner, and dashboard, with evidence timestamps and per-surface states (reachable, authorized, observable, actionable).
A hard guard in action execution that refuses to label UI steps successful when Accessibility/inputReachability is false.
An explicit browser pending-command policy: inspect, retry, or discard only after owner confirmation.
A small pendant/relay status verb so the owner can hear the result without opening the dashboard.

args.change: Add a read-only preflight/evidence envelope to every cross-surface job. Immediately before execution, snapshot Mac permission/input reachability, screen-observation availability, browser extension heartbeat and pending-command count, relay/pendant link state, and relevant session freshness. Attach the envelope and its timestamp to the job; after execution, require a postcondition observation (or explicitly mark unverifiable) before a receipt can say completed. Keep the existing action APIs, but make the envelope mandatory input to planner and dashboard.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets an honest answer when the machine cannot be acted on: 'browser offline, 2 commands waiting' or 'Accessibility missing; nothing was changed' instead of a misleading success. When it does work, the receipt says what was observed afterward, not merely what the agent attempted.
args.effort: Medium: typed schema, Mac/relay collectors, job persistence, planner integration, and dashboard rendering; one to two implementation cycles.
args.risk: Status can become stale between preflight and click, or a postcondition may be impossible for actions like sending an email. Recover by timestamping every field, distinguishing observed/assumed/unverifiable, and using idempotency plus the existing undo path. Never block reversible non-UI work solely because screen observation is unavailable.
args.cost_impact: Negligible API cost; a few hundred bytes per job in D1 and occasional status requests. No hardware cost.
args.latency_impact: Adds roughly 100–500 ms for local checks and up to one heartbeat round trip; postcondition checks may add 0.5–2 s only for UI jobs.
args.security_impact: Improves safety by preventing false success. Must redact private URLs, tokens, screenshots, and secret capture values from shared envelopes; retain only capability booleans, timestamps, and reason codes.
depends_on: A shared typed context/preflight contract across relay, Mac planner, browser runner, and dashboard
A hard action-layer rule preventing success receipts when uiActionsWillReachTheScreen=false
An explicit policy for browser pending commands and unverifiable postconditions

transcript.text:
Recorded a new capability: **offline continuity catch-up**.

The owner should be able to ask, “What happened while you were offline?” and receive a deduplicated spoken summary of held alerts, bookmarks, delayed replies, and available audio—with timestamps, delivery state, replay controls, and per-item acknowledgement.

It requires:

- A shared continuity-event schema across pendant microSD, relay D1, Mac pipeline, and dashboard.
- Stable event IDs, content hashes, clock-skew handling, and idempotent acknowledgement.
- Pendant commands for listing, acknowledging, and replaying events.
- Resumable audio retrieval and retention rules.
- A spoken catch-up intent and dashboard timeline for unacknowledged or newly delivered events.
- Privacy controls for sensitive offline recordings and messages.

Fresh observations recorded:

- **Critical contradiction:** owner memory says `America/Chicago`; live Mac reports `America/New_York`. Time-sensitive calendar, reminder, and “what time is it?” actions are unsafe until the owner confirms the authoritative timezone.

- **24 kHz audio server leg works:** Mac generated 24 kHz mono PCM with no clipping and uploaded it to the relay. Pendant speaker playback remains unverified.

I proposed a new **perception-health compiler** connecting `/machine-context`, `/observe`, `/ops/status`, `/browser/status`, and relay telemetry. It would detect stale or contradictory state, warn the pendant before risky answers, and prevent false UI-completion claims.

What I still need:

1. **Owner confirmation of the authoritative timezone** (Chicago or New York).
2. **A live browser heartbeat** before authenticated-page work can be trusted.
3. **Pendant-side playback telemetry or a physical playback test** to establish the remaining half of the 24 kHz path.
4. **Accessibility and Screen Recording grants for the exact running AI Pendant Agent binary** if reliable GUI interaction is required; this cannot be granted from inside the harness.

args.user_asks: Did I actually hear the last thing you sent me? If not, tell me exactly where delivery stopped and offer to replay only the missing audio.
args.why_useful: Today the system can prove that Mac rendered 24 kHz audio and the relay accepted it, but it cannot distinguish queued, downloaded, played, interrupted, or never-heard on the pendant. The owner needs an honest answer rather than a false completion claim, especially for reminders and safety-relevant briefings.
args.model_tier: background state machine and deterministic receipts; realtime model only for the owner's short spoken question and explanation
args.latency_budget: Under 500 ms for a cached answer; under 2 s after requesting a fresh pendant status; replay begins as soon as the missing segment is identified
args.cost_estimate: Negligible metadata storage and relay traffic; no model call for normal state transitions, with a small text-model call only for ambiguous interruptions
args.security_concerns: Store audio identifiers and timing, not transcript or raw audio in the receipt. Do not infer that sound was heard from DAC start alone; expose uncertainty. Replaying private content requires the pendant to remain paired to the owner.
missing: Pendant firmware playback lifecycle events: downloaded, decoder-started, DAC-started, paused, interrupted, completed, and local failure reason
A durable per-audio delivery state machine spanning relay upload/download and pendant playback acknowledgements
A replay-from-last-unheard-segment command with deduplication and expiry
A clear distinction between physical playback and confirmed human hearing

args.change: Add a cross-surface 'witness ledger' that assigns one event ID and monotonic sequence to each pendant utterance, relay receipt, Mac planning result, browser command, audio render, download, and physical button interruption. Each node appends only signed facts with its own clock and uncertainty; the relay reconciles them into a causal timeline without pretending wall-clock agreement. Expose a query that returns the last known state and the exact missing acknowledgement for any owner request.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can ask 'what happened?' and receive a truthful causal account even when the Mac timezone differs, the browser is offline, or the pendant reconnects late. It prevents a server receipt from being mistaken for an action or a rendered file from being mistaken for something heard.
args.effort: High: protocol/schema design, firmware flash-persistent sequence counter, relay append-only storage, Mac/browser adapters, clock-skew reconciliation, and dashboard rendering.
args.risk: Extra writes and complex reconciliation could consume pendant flash or create duplicate events after power loss. Bound the local journal, use idempotent event IDs, and mark uncertain ordering instead of guessing; rotate and expire sensitive payload references.
args.cost_impact: Small relay D1/R2 metadata growth and occasional telemetry bytes; no additional inference cost. Pendant firmware needs a few kilobytes of journal metadata and wear-levelled flash writes.
args.latency_impact: No added latency on the hot voice path if events are buffered locally; timeline queries may take 1–2 seconds while reconnecting nodes flush journals.
args.security_impact: The ledger must contain opaque content hashes and metadata rather than transcripts, URLs, or secrets; encrypt in transit and limit owner-visible history. A tamper-evident chain improves auditability but must not be marketed as proof that the owner heard audio.
depends_on: A firmware-persistent monotonic event counter and bounded journal
Relay append-only event ingestion and deduplication
Mac/browser adapters emitting lifecycle facts
A shared causal-event schema with clock uncertainty

args.user_asks: “I have to leave now—hand this unfinished task to whichever device can continue it, and when I come back tell me exactly where it stopped, what is already done, and what still needs my approval.”
args.why_useful: Today work is split across a live pendant conversation, relay jobs, Mac execution, and private browser sessions, but an interruption can strand the task or cause the next surface to repeat steps. The owner needs a single resumable handoff that preserves the exact checkpoint, evidence, pending approvals, and prohibited repeats across devices. args.model_tier: Use deterministic checkpointing and typed state transitions first. A cheap background model may summarize the checkpoint; realtime is only needed when the owner asks for the spoken handoff or resumes interactively.
args.latency_budget: Checkpoint on disconnect or explicit 'leave it' within 1 second; resume preparation within 5 seconds after another surface appears. Never execute a pending irreversible step automatically during handoff.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero model cost for checkpoint persistence and reconciliation; approximately $0.001–$0.01 for a concise background summary. Storage and state reconciliation dominate, not inference.
args.security_concerns: The checkpoint may contain private browser URLs, form contents, email drafts, or calendar data. Encrypt sensitive fields, bind checkpoints to the paired owner and task, expire abandoned checkpoints, and require explicit approval before any irreversible continuation. Never copy credentials or raw secrets into the pendant.
missing: A durable task-checkpoint schema spanning relay, Mac jobs, browser sessions, pipeline events, and action receipts
Per-step idempotency and a do-not-repeat ledger that records whether a step was attempted, verified, or only staged
A resumability state machine with explicit interruption, waiting-for-owner, expired, resumed, and abandoned states
A cross-surface handoff protocol so the pendant can park work and the Mac/browser can resume it without relying on transcript text
A compact checkpoint renderer that can speak the stopping point and pending approval without exposing private page contents

args.change: Introduce a cross-surface resumable-task protocol, not another job queue: each in-progress task gets an append-only checkpoint containing a task graph, last verified postcondition, staged-but-uncommitted mutations, owner-approval tokens, and idempotency keys. The relay can atomically park the checkpoint when pendant connectivity drops; Mac and browser agents can lease it, resume only from the last verified node, and return a signed handoff receipt. A do-not-repeat ledger must reject replay of an attempted step unless its postcondition is proven absent. Expire leases and surface unresolved checkpoints to the pendant as a short spoken status.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner can walk away from a task without losing the exact stopping point or risking duplicate submissions. They return to a truthful, actionable handoff instead of reconstructing state from a transcript or guessing whether a browser/Mac action happened.
args.effort: High: shared protocol and persistence across relay D1, Mac job tracker, browser session bridge, pipeline telemetry, and receipt/journal formats; failure-injection tests for link loss, duplicate delivery, stale leases, and partial form submission.
args.risk: A bad postcondition could incorrectly permit a repeat or block legitimate recovery. Default to blocked/unknown when evidence is insufficient, require approval tokens for irreversible steps, and preserve every checkpoint transition for audit and manual recovery.
args.cost_impact: Small durable-state and D1/storage cost per active task; negligible inference cost. Optional summarization is background-tier only.
args.latency_impact: Parking is sub-second; resume adds a few seconds to revalidate browser/session state and compare postconditions before action.
args.security_impact: Checkpoints must be encrypted and scoped to the paired owner/task; redact form values and URLs in spoken output; never persist credentials or raw private-page bodies; revoke leases on pairing changes.
depends_on: A typed cross-surface task graph and immutable correlation IDs
Action-specific postcondition verification, especially a safe alternative when GUI Accessibility is unavailable
Durable owner-approval tokens that cannot be replayed
Relay-side lease/expiry and recovery semantics
Browser and Mac adapters that expose staged versus committed state

- **Timezone:** confirmed as `America/New_York`.
- **Audio/pipeline:** a completed response was rendered at 24 kHz mono PCM and accepted by the relay. The pipeline also records two offline-held alerts being surfaced from pendant storage, plus a successful 15,625 Hz native-audio upload.

What I still need:

1. **Direct pendant diagnostics and continuity snapshot access** — current firmware state, connectivity, queue contents, acknowledgement semantics, and whether held alerts are safely deduplicated.
2. **Current offline-capture integrity status** — whether recordings/events survive LTE drops and reboots without duplication or loss.
3. **Browser-extension recovery state** — why Chrome is offline and what the queued commands represent before anyone attempts replay.
4. **A resolution of the GUI-permission constraint** from the owner. I cannot establish trustworthy screen interaction until Accessibility and Screen Recording are granted to the exact running AI Pendant Agent binary; I will not treat synthetic UI receipts as evidence meanwhile.

The most important unknown is the pendant’s actual current state: the server shows historical and pipeline-level evidence, but I still cannot directly verify the device’s live queue, firmware health, or continuity state.

args.user_asks: When I say “did you hear me, and did I hear your reply?”, give me a trustworthy end-to-end receipt for that conversation turn—showing what the pendant captured, what the relay received, what the Mac produced, what audio was delivered, and any gap or duplicate—without pretending delivery means playback.
args.why_useful: Today the system has separate evidence in pendant-originated pipeline events, relay jobs, Mac logs, and generated audio, but the owner cannot answer the basic question “was that exchange actually completed?” A reconciled chain-of-custody receipt would expose silent LTE drops, stale queued replies, duplicate forwarding, and the crucial distinction between rendered, downloaded, and physically played audio.
args.model_tier: Use a cheap background model (gpt-5.6-luna or equivalent) only to reconcile already-structured events; reserve gpt-realtime-2.1 for the live turn and do not resend raw audio to the reconciliation model.
args.latency_budget: Generate incrementally after a turn or reconnect; a preliminary receipt within 2 seconds and a finalized receipt after late device acknowledgements. Never delay live speech.
args.cost_estimate: Low: one small structured reconciliation call per completed or recovered turn; dominated by event/context tokens, not audio. Raw PCM should remain out of the model path.
args.security_concerns: Receipts may contain private speech metadata, timestamps, and logged-in-session references. Keep them in the existing authenticated D1/dashboard path, redact transcript text by default, hash audio rather than exposing it, and require confirmation before exporting or sharing a receipt.
missing: A shared conversation-turn identifier propagated from pendant capture through relay job, Mac pipeline, TTS artifact, download, and local playback acknowledgement
A pendant-originated playback-start/playback-complete acknowledgement with monotonic sequence and interruption reason
A reconciler that joins late and duplicate events without treating server acceptance as physical delivery
A dashboard and spoken query that display confidence and explicitly label unknown stages

args.user_asks: Keep me uninterrupted while I’m focused, but don’t make me miss something genuinely urgent: infer my current attention state from the pendant, Mac, calendar, and browser, hold ordinary notifications, and surface only urgency-qualified items with the reason they broke through.
args.why_useful: The owner currently gets disconnected alert handling and ordinary automation, but no single attention policy that understands whether they are in a meeting, presenting, coding, asleep, or merely away from the Mac. This would make the pendant a respectful gatekeeper instead of another notification channel, while preserving an auditable explanation for every interruption.
args.model_tier: Use deterministic rules and a small background model for urgency classification and summarization; use gpt-realtime-2.1 only when the pendant actually speaks to the owner.
args.latency_budget: State changes within 5 seconds of a Mac/calendar/browser signal; urgent alert decision within 2 seconds; ordinary alerts can wait for a scheduled digest.
args.cost_estimate: Low to moderate: mostly event filtering and one small classifier call per candidate alert; no audio or page contents need leave the Mac unless required for classification.
args.security_concerns: This observes foreground apps, meeting times, browser account notifications, and possibly presence patterns. Keep raw page text and app titles local where possible, send only a sensitivity-tagged urgency fact to the relay, provide a visible pause switch, and never let the classifier bypass explicit safety categories without a user-defined policy.
missing: A shared attention-state contract with states such as available, focused, meeting, asleep, and away, including source, confidence, expiry, and user override
A unified notification inbox that accepts Mac, browser, relay, and pendant events with urgency, sensitivity, deduplication, and quiet-hours metadata
A local browser notification reader that can classify urgency without uploading private page contents
A pendant acknowledgement protocol distinguishing surfaced, heard, dismissed, and deferred alerts

args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner would receive and acknowledge alerts without looking at a screen or speaking aloud, and the system could stop claiming that an alert was noticed merely because it was downloaded. args.latency_impact: Sub-100 ms local acknowledgement and immediate tactile alerting, avoiding LTE round trips. No model latency for basic patterns.
args.security_impact: Motion and wear state are sensitive presence signals. Keep raw sensor data on-device, export only coarse state with explicit retention, and never infer location from it.
depends_on: A firmware event schema for local acknowledgement and worn-state transitions

transcript.text:
Recorded a new capability: **auditable audible delivery**.

The owner should be able to ask, “Did that actually reach my ears?” and receive a truthful distinction between audio rendered, uploaded, downloaded, playback started, playback completed, and likely heard. If delivery was interrupted, the system should replay only the unacknowledged portion.

This requires:

- Pendant firmware playback receipts with utterance IDs, byte ranges, interruptions, underruns, mute state, and monotonic timestamps.
- Durable relay receipt reconciliation and deduplication.
- Perception rules that never equate “relay accepted audio” with “owner heard it.”
- Gap-aware replay, with privacy-safe metadata and no microphone recordings.

args.user_asks: “When my pendant, Mac, or browser comes back online, tell me what happened while it was disconnected, reconcile any actions whose outcome is uncertain, and show me only the items that need my confirmation.”
args.why_useful: Today the system can queue work and report receipts, but it cannot give one trustworthy answer when different nodes disappear at different times. This would turn offline periods into a safe, understandable handoff: the relay supplies durable events, the Mac supplies local job receipts and observations, and the browser supplies authenticated-page evidence when its extension reconnects. It explicitly distinguishes confirmed success, confirmed failure, and unknown outcome instead of treating a queued command as completed.
args.model_tier: background for periodic reconciliation and event classification; deterministic for connectivity/state joins; planner only when evidence conflicts or an action's outcome needs interpretation. Realtime is used only to read the concise resulting card aloud when the pendant is actually connected.
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds for deterministic connectivity and receipt joins after reconnect; under 15 seconds for a background reconciliation pass; no planner call unless conflicts remain. The owner should receive a compact spoken summary plus a review queue, not a long transcript.
args.cost_estimate: Usually near-zero model cost for event joins and hashes; roughly one gpt-4.1-mini call (about 2–4k input tokens) only for conflicting evidence, with a planner escalation only for genuinely ambiguous cases. Dominant cost is retained event metadata and occasional browser/Mac re-observation, not realtime inference.
args.security_concerns: Private browser URLs, page snippets, Mac receipts, and relay event IDs leave their originating node only as redacted evidence summaries. Keep secrets and page bodies local; encrypt event records; attach source, timestamp, node identity, and freshness to every claim. Never infer success from command enqueue alone. Any retry, resend, cancellation, or browser submission requires explicit confirmation and an idempotency key.
missing: A shared append-only cross-node event envelope with monotonic per-node sequence numbers, wall-clock plus monotonic timestamps, and delivery acknowledgements
A reconciliation endpoint that can correlate relay jobs, Mac jobs/receipts, browser command IDs, and pendant connectivity epochs without declaring unknown outcomes successful
Browser extension reconnect replay and acknowledgement of the 9 currently pending commands before any automatic cleanup
A compact review-queue/card surface and a pendant reconnect notification path; there is no pendant currently registered, so this cannot be exercised end-to-end yet

args.change: Add a cross-node evidence-quorum verifier for every mutating job. Before a job is considered complete, require an authenticated relay delivery record plus a surface-specific postcondition: Mac jobs must provide a typed local receipt and read-back state; browser mutations must provide commandId/session/tab affinity and a post-action DOM or page-state fingerprint; future pendant-originated actions must provide a device sequence and relay acknowledgement. If the nodes disagree or a postcondition cannot be read, persist status=unknown with the exact missing evidence and never auto-retry. On reconnect, replay and close the quorum using idempotency keys.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner stops hearing confident “done” when only a command was queued or a disconnected browser may have submitted it. They get a truthful three-way result—confirmed, failed, or unknown—with a concrete next check, preventing duplicate purchases, messages, form submissions, and reminders.
args.effort: Medium-high: define a versioned evidence envelope and idempotency contract in relay and Mac job storage; add browser postcondition capture; implement deterministic verifier and dashboard/review cards; migrate existing receipts conservatively as unknown when evidence is insufficient.
args.risk: Some previously reported jobs will downgrade to unknown, which may surprise the owner; no action is undone automatically. A malformed or stale postcondition could falsely confirm, so enforce source signatures, freshness windows, and schema validation. Recover by retaining raw evidence and allowing a manual re-check.
args.cost_impact: Negligible per-job compute/storage for hashes and metadata; occasional extra read-back request per mutation. Conflict resolution may use a small background-model call, but the common path is deterministic.
args.latency_impact: Adds roughly 0.2–2 seconds for local/browser read-back; long-running jobs remain asynchronous. If a node is offline, completion waits for reconnect rather than guessing.
args.security_impact: Improves safety by minimizing page/body transfer and binding evidence to node, session, tab, job, and timestamp. Evidence metadata still reveals activity, so encrypt at rest and redact URLs/snippets according to sensitivity.
depends_on: A shared append-only event/evidence envelope across relay, Mac, and browser
Stable idempotency keys and typed postcondition readers for Mac and browser actions
A review surface that exposes unknown outcomes without silently retrying
Pendant registration and device sequence acknowledgements before pendant-originated evidence can be verified

args.user_asks: “For any task, show me exactly what information crossed between my pendant, Mac, browser, and relay—what was retained, for how long, and what was never sent—and let me erase the task’s remote traces without breaking my local receipts.”
args.why_useful: The owner cannot currently audit the privacy boundary of a multi-surface action. They should be able to distinguish audio that stayed local from audio or page text sent to the relay, see which snippets were included in model context, and delete remotely retained material while preserving a minimal local proof that the task happened. This is a user-facing privacy capability, not merely logs: it answers “what did you learn about me, where is it now, and can I remove it?” across the whole hive.
args.model_tier: Deterministic event accounting and redaction manifests on every task; background model only to turn the manifest into a short plain-language explanation. No realtime model call except when the owner asks verbally through a connected pendant.
args.latency_budget: A manifest should be available within 1 second of task completion; a spoken explanation within 5 seconds. Erasure should return a verifiable receipt within 10 seconds, with local-only cleanup continuing asynchronously if necessary.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero inference cost for manifests, hashes, retention metadata, and deletion receipts. A small gpt-4.1-mini call (about 1–2k tokens) is optional for natural-language explanation. Storage overhead is a few hundred bytes per event plus hashes, not page or audio bodies.
args.security_concerns: The audit itself is sensitive and must be access-controlled, encrypted, and careful not to duplicate the secret it describes. Store content hashes, classifications, destinations, model/provider, retention deadline, and user-visible excerpts only where consented. Erasure must be cryptographically scoped by task and refuse to claim deletion from third-party systems it cannot control; preserve tamper-evident local receipts without recoverable content.
missing: A mandatory cross-node data-lineage envelope recording source surface, destination, field classification, model/provider, purpose, retention deadline, and content hash for every transfer
Relay APIs for task-scoped export, deletion, and deletion receipts across D1/R2/audio artifacts
Mac and browser middleware that emits lineage events before sending page text, screenshots, audio, or action results
A local privacy ledger and owner-facing redaction/erase UI, plus a pendant command when a pendant is eventually registered

args.user_asks: “Before I rely on it, tell me what parts of my AI system are really reachable right now, what is merely queued or stale, and what evidence supports each answer.”
args.why_useful: Today the fleet reports contradictory truths: the Mac bridge is online while its browser extension is offline with nine pending commands; durable browser sessions remain listed without an attached tab; and pipeline records can remain processing or approval-blocked for hours. A perception-first reachability brief prevents the owner from believing an action happened, or exposing private browser work to a nonexistent connection. It is genuinely cross-node: only the relay can compare delivery records, the Mac can inspect local sessions and permissions, and the browser can confirm attachment.
args.model_tier: background: deterministic reconciliation and a cheap text model for the brief; realtime only when the owner asks verbally for an immediate status.
args.latency_budget: Under 2 seconds for cached status; up to 10 seconds for fresh Mac/browser heartbeats. Never claim fresh evidence if a surface does not answer.
args.cost_estimate: Usually near-zero model cost for typed status aggregation; roughly $0.001–$0.01 only when a short model-generated explanation is requested. Main cost is context transfer from status records, capped to changed records.
args.security_concerns: Do not include private tab URLs, page text, or tokens in the spoken brief unless explicitly requested. Report capability class and evidence timestamps. Pending browser commands must be labeled and never replayed by this read-only capability. Require confirmation before any attempted reconnect or retry.
missing: A typed cross-surface reconciliation record with observedAt, source, freshness TTL, and state vocabulary (reachable, attached, queued, executing, delivered, approval-blocked, stale, unknown).
A relay endpoint that joins Mac job/pipeline records with browser heartbeat/command state and device registry without copying page contents.
Browser extension reconnect/heartbeat implementation; currently home-chrome is offline.
Pendant registration and delivery acknowledgements; no pendant is currently registered.
Owner-granted Accessibility and Screen Recording for com.aipendant.agent if GUI reachability is to be reported as ready.

args.change: Add a read-only fleet truth ledger and reconciler. Every observation from relay device registry, Mac /ops/status and /observe, browser heartbeat/poll, jobs/receipts, and pipeline events becomes a typed fact {surface, objectId, state, observedAt, source, evidenceHash, expiresAt}. Reconcile contradictory states without overwriting evidence: e.g. browser session=present but extension=offline => session detached; pipeline=processing beyond TTL => stale, not running; local action=approval-blocked => not delivered. Expose a compact diff endpoint and emit a change event only when a fact crosses state or freshness boundaries.
args.why_useful_to_owner: The owner gets honest answers about whether something is reachable, queued, actually executed, or merely an old record. It stops the most dangerous failure mode in a personal assistant: a success-looking receipt when the screen was never touched or a pendant never received the result.
args.effort: Medium: shared schema, relay D1 tables/queries, Mac adapter, browser heartbeat adapter, TTL policy, tests with offline and delayed-delivery fixtures. No GUI permission required for the read-only ledger.
args.risk: Incorrect TTLs could label slow work stale or create noisy transitions. Preserve raw observations, show evidence timestamps, use conservative unknown after expiry, and make the ledger read-only so reconciliation cannot trigger retries or actions.
args.cost_impact: Negligible storage/compute per event; a few D1 rows per state transition. No model call for reconciliation; optional summary generation is low-cost background text.
args.latency_impact: Cached reads under 100 ms; fresh reconciliation adds one heartbeat interval, normally 1–3 seconds. It should never delay execution paths.
args.security_impact: Store hashes and metadata by default, not private page text or audio. Restrict the ledger to the owner bearer token; redact URLs/titles in spoken output unless requested.
depends_on: A single authoritative device-registry contract and delivery acknowledgement semantics.
Stable job/pipeline IDs and idempotent event ingestion.
Browser extension heartbeat/reconnect; currently extension is offline.
Owner Accessibility/Screen Recording grants only if the ledger is later extended to assert GUI input reachability.

args.user_asks: “Show me a tamper-evident timeline of what I said, what each node received, what it decided, what it tried, and what reached me—including gaps while I was offline—and let me export that incident report.”
args.why_useful: Today a stale pipeline record, a relay acknowledgement, a Mac receipt, and a pendant playback can look like the same event even when they are not. The owner cannot independently answer whether a spoken request was transcribed, acted on, delivered, played, or lost during a disconnect. A causal, gap-aware timeline gives them a trustworthy answer after the fact without silently retrying or changing anything. This is not a task runner, page watcher, briefing, or generic job-status view: it is an evidence export spanning the wearable, relay, Mac, and browser, including explicit unknown intervals.
args.model_tier: Deterministic event stitching and hashing first; use a cheap background text model only to render a human-readable incident summary. Realtime is unnecessary.
args.latency_budget: Export a recent incident in under 3 seconds from indexed records; historical reconstruction may take 10 seconds. Missing evidence must be shown as a gap, never inferred.
args.cost_estimate: Near-zero inference cost for the structured timeline; approximately $0.001–$0.01 for optional prose. Storage and indexing of compact event metadata dominate, not model calls.
args.security_concerns: The export may contain private speech transcripts, URLs, action parameters, and device identifiers. Encrypt at rest, scope access to the owner's bearer/session, redact payloads by default, offer a metadata-only export, and require explicit confirmation before sharing or uploading an incident report. Hashes prove record continuity, not truth of an untrusted source, so show source and trust level.
missing: A cross-node event envelope with globally unique event IDs, parent/causal IDs, monotonic sequence numbers per device, source identity, observed time, received time, and explicit event type.
Relay-issued connection epochs and delivery/playback acknowledgements binding a response to a registered device; late, duplicated, simulated, and historical events must be distinct states.
Mac and browser adapters that append signed/hashed receipts rather than only human-readable job status; browser tab/session identifiers must be privacy-redactable.
An append-only encrypted event store plus a verifier/export route that preserves missing intervals and detects duplicates, rewrites, and clock disagreement.
A user-facing incident viewer/audio transcript redaction workflow on the Mac dashboard and a concise spoken answer on the relay.

args.change: Create a cross-node causal event journal distinct from execution receipts: pendant, relay, Mac, and browser each append hash-linked envelopes with local monotonic sequence, parent event ID, connection epoch, observed/received timestamps, and trust class. The relay periodically seals batches; a verifier detects missing ranges, duplicate IDs, clock conflicts, and post-hoc edits, then produces a redacted incident export with explicit UNKNOWN gaps. Keep payloads encrypted and optional; metadata-only verification must work.
args.why_useful_to_owner: After a disconnect or surprising action, the owner can prove what actually happened and where the chain broke instead of choosing between contradictory status screens. They get an honest incident report, including “no evidence of playback,” rather than a confident but false success.
args.effort: High: protocol/schema shared by firmware source, relay D1, Mac agent, and browser bridge; append-only storage, key rotation, export verifier, dashboard viewer, and simulated loss/duplication tests.
args.risk: More metadata can expose behavior patterns and clock conflicts can create confusing reports. Default to local encryption and redaction, retain raw evidence only for a configurable period, label source trust explicitly, and never let verification trigger retries or actions.
args.cost_impact: Small per-event storage/index cost and occasional batch hashing; no model cost. Larger exports may incur encrypted storage/network cost only when the owner requests them.
args.latency_impact: Append is asynchronous and should add under 20 ms to normal processing; sealing/export is background. No impact on realtime speech path.
args.security_impact: Improves tamper detection but introduces signing keys and sensitive event metadata. Keep keys device-scoped, rotate/revoke on pairing changes, prevent the relay from decrypting payloads by default, and require owner confirmation for any remote export.
depends_on: A stable pairing identity and connection-epoch protocol for the future pendant.
Relay persistence and authenticated Mac/browser event ingestion.
A defined retention/redaction policy and owner-visible verifier UI.
The currently absent physical pendant must be connected before pendant-side signatures and playback evidence can be validated.
